mathematical_findings.finding: Full-domain IntegrableOn is a conclusion. A tolerance-1 invocation of the proved uniform actual closed small-z tail supplies a cutoff with finite integral of the absolute actual kernel. Measurability gives AEStronglyMeasurable. The complement above h has finite volume and the actual compact pointwise bound. The two sets cover every original closed ordered point; overlap at z=h is harmless for integrability union.

The public physical and ideal integrability wrappers reduce to the two literal WallKernel branches. Physical quantifies all m and e in [0,1/384]; the ideal is the true GatedKernel with its supplied buffer, and the later limit instantiates buffer zero.

FiniteFunctional integrates the actual finite lookup over the complete original closed order region. IdealFunctional is the literal OrderedKernel at buffer zero on the closed manuscript old-cube tail region. Their bridge uses the existing pointwise manuscript indicator identity, including the proved zero equality face, rather than assuming a null wall or identifying different kernels.

The difference of real integrals is legally rewritten as the integral of the difference using the newly derived full-domain IntegrableOn facts. The fixed Mathlib norm-integral inequality then bounds its absolute value by the toReal of precisely the existing full absolute difference mass.

For every positive epsilon, the inherited full L1 theorem constructs e0 and m0 before all later e,m. The e0 cap supplies the integrability range. ENNReal.toReal_mono uses the finite upper bound ofReal epsilon, so infinity is not silently mapped to zero. The result is a uniform analytic functional approximation.
